_meta.what_this_is: Three study conditions over the same set of items, differing only in how many items the learner ATTEMPTS as a test BEFORE studying (a pretest they will mostly fail, because they have not learned the material yet). study_only pretests none; pretest_half pretests half; pretest_all pretests every item. Then all conditions study every item, and all take the same delayed test.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE, and the model is a STYLIZED but faithful account of a robust, replicated finding: attempting a test before instruction -- even with wrong answers -- improves later retention of the studied material (the pretesting / errorful-generation effect). Constants: study_gain is the delayed-test accuracy from studying alone; max_pretest_boost is the extra delayed-test accuracy when every item was pretested first; pretest_immediate_accuracy is how well the pretest itself is answered (low -- the learner has not studied yet). Every score is computed in pretest.py from the pretested counts and these constants.
_meta.format: n_items: int; model: {study_gain, max_pretest_boost, pretest_immediate_accuracy}; conditions: [{name, pretested}].
